claims.text: Laser cladding a high-entropy-alloy coating onto critical steel components enhances their surface physical and mechanical characteristics in aggressive environments.
Untreated 316L stainless steel or H13 steel has moderate hardness and wear resistance and is susceptible to corrosion under high-temperature or saline conditions.
An AlCoCrFeNi-type high-entropy alloy can be deposited onto a steel surface by laser cladding.
The proposed coating is intended to remain effective at temperatures up to about 900 °C and in corrosive environments such as sulfate-chloride molten salts or salty atmospheres.
Laser cladding produces a robust metallurgical bond between the coating and substrate.
The laser-cladded high-entropy-alloy coating is dense and has low porosity.
Rapid solidification forms either an FCC-BCC dual-phase microstructure or a precipitate-strengthened microstructure in the coating.
The rapid heating and cooling inherent to laser cladding produces a refined microstructure.
The refined microstructure increases hardness through precipitation strengthening.
Phase stability in the coating contributes to enhanced hardness.
The increased coating hardness improves wear resistance.
The proposed refined and strengthened microstructure improves corrosion resistance.
The proposed refined and strengthened microstructure improves resistance to thermal degradation.
The coated components will have approximately 20–40% greater surface hardness than untreated substrates.
The coating will reduce wear relative to an untreated steel baseline.
The coating will reduce corrosion relative to an untreated steel baseline.
The expected improvement depends on production of a homogeneous, defect-free coating.
The expected improvement applies only while temperature, corrosive species, and stress remain within a validated operating range.
The magnitude of improvement varies with laser-cladding parameters, coating composition, and environmental conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if coated samples fail to achieve a statistically significant hardness increase of about 20% and a wear or corrosion rate reduction of about 30% relative to untreated controls.
